A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Persuasive Privacy by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the retained definitions, propositions, and proofs can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 presents a theoretical framework, mathematical proofs, and an analytical guarantee for releasing an empirical average. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 adds theoretical privacy definitions, derivations, and a cell-suppression example with a proof. Neither its main text nor its appendices report original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix C introduces Persuasive Privacy in Expectation: Assumption 4* replaces the tail-probability criterion with an expectation of a transformed privacy score, adding a substantive alternative assessment procedure. The original PP framework remains, and Section 5.2 adds a cell-suppression instantiation with its own score and prior class.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The added count-vector example is analytical and does not establish new evaluated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates experimental baselines. The added comparisons with Rényi DP, quantitative information flow, and pufferfish privacy are formal or conceptual comparisons.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, sample sizes, or testing procedures. The new privacy parameters specify mathematical guarantees.

E4.justification: No ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, or empirical case studies are reported. The added cell-suppression guarantee and its proof are theoretical additions assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Bayesian uncertainty and privacy failure probabilities are components of the theory, not empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Neither version reports measured numerical outcomes, experimental rankings, or observed qualitative findings. Added equivalences and corrected symbolic bounds are theoretical changes assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds PPE definitions and Propositions 11–13 connecting it to Rényi DP and f-divergence privacy; Section 5.2 and Appendix E.7 add the cell-suppression proposition and proof. Proposition 3 now requires conjugacy only to M1. Appendix A corrects the log-score sign and distinguishes countably supported distributions from two-point distributions. The PDP proof is rewritten, and the retained mean theorem's proof ends with r1 + log(r2), correcting v1's inconsistent r1 - log(r2).

C1.justification: The abstract and central game-theoretic privacy claims remain unchanged. The introduction and conclusion extend the stated contributions to Rényi DP and f-divergence privacy through modified assumptions, while the introduction narrows the deterministic-mechanism contrast from DP and its variants to DP and most variants.

C2.justification: New Appendix D develops substantive interpretations contrasting PP with QIF's averaging and pufferfish's mechanism stability. Section 5.2 acknowledges the strong cell-independence assumption. The conclusion newly admits that systematic context-specific score selection remains undemonstrated and discusses misuse through inappropriate scores or prior classes.

D1.justification: No implementation, computational settings, hardware, runtime, code release, or data-access information is added. The new mechanism parameters and formulas specify theoretical constructions rather than implementation or experimental reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Appendix D substantially expands positioning against QIF, differential privacy, pufferfish, and noiseless privacy, including distinctions absent from v1's brief citations. Newly cited work includes Mironov (2017), Alvim et al. (2012; 2020), Bhaskar et al. (2011), and Pan et al. (2025).

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are retained. Local explanations and the conclusion are revised, Section 5 gains named subsections, and new Appendices C–D move the existing proof appendix from C to E. Affiliations, acknowledgements, and publication text also change.

P2.justification: Neither version contains figures or tables. Visual changes include the revised first-page affiliation and conference footer, reformatted proof displays, and associated text reflow; the two-column main text and single-column appendix format remain.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects mathematical inconsistencies, revises the PDP proof, and substantially improves discussion of prior work and limitations. However, new Proposition 13 equates an ordinary PPE expectation with a full f-divergence by assigning a singular-mass contribution to zero-density outcomes. Definition 10 does not explain this change to ordinary expectation, leaving the claimed general equivalence insufficiently justified. These gains and the substantive new proof concern prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
